Data Appreciation · Week 10 · Title

Bias in data and in AI

Data reflects who was counted. When people are missing from the data, decisions and AI trained on it fail them.

Next Generation Genius · Year 1 · Foundation

Data Appreciation · Week 10 · Goals

By the end of today

  • Explain how missing people make data biased
  • Show how an AI model learns bias from its training data
  • Suggest how to make data fairer
Data Appreciation · Week 10 · Idea 1

Understand it

Data only describes the people who were counted. If a survey of "young people" is done only online, those without a phone are missing — and their needs vanish from the decision.

AI is trained on data, so it learns the gaps. A face-recognition system trained mostly on light-skinned faces makes more mistakes on dark-skinned faces. Nothing in the program is "racist"; the training data was not fair.

Whenever you see data, ask: who is missing? who decided what to count? who benefits? The fix is usually better data — more people, more kinds of people — not a cleverer program.

Data Appreciation · Week 10 · Key words

Key words

Training data
the examples an AI system learns from
Representative
the sample looks like the population
Algorithmic bias
unfair results from biased data or design
Data Appreciation · Week 10 · Practice

Now you do it

  1. Train a Teachable Machine model on a lopsided set
  2. Test it on examples it never saw
  3. Fix the data and test again

Need a hand? Do the Teachable Machine activity with a partner and talk through each test.

Done early? Research one real case of AI bias and present it in five sentences.

Data Appreciation · Week 10 · Assessment

How you will be assessed

  • Train a Teachable Machine model with lopsided examples, test it, then fix the data. Paste your result and say what changed.
  • An AI tool trained mostly on English voices often misunderstands Nigerian accents. What is the main cause?

Your work is marked against the rubric, and you may be asked to explain your choices. Show your own thinking.
